previous_statement: Compressed-space identity: def-compressed-corner gives S_{P,Q}=Im Co_{P,Q} and S_{P_n,Q_n}=Im Co_{P_n,Q_n}. For every linear T:A->A, Im(iota_n(T)) consists exactly of matrices [T(X_ij)], hence equals M_n tensor Im(T): inclusion from left to right is entrywise, while for [Y_ij] with each Y_ij in Im(T), choose X_ij with T(X_ij)=Y_ij and assemble [X_ij]. Applying this to T=Co_{P,Q} and the preceding compression-map identity yields S_{P_n,Q_n}=M_n tensor S_{P,Q}.
new_statement: Image-amplification lemma and its limitation: for every linear map T:A->A, Im(iota_n(T))=M_n tensor Im(T), since iota_n(T) acts entrywise and arbitrary entrywise preimages can be assembled into a matrix. Therefore the implication Co_{P_n,Q_n}=iota_n(Co_{P,Q}) implies S_{P_n,Q_n}=M_n tensor S_{P,Q}, using S_{R,S}=Im Co_{R,S} from def-compressed-corner. However node 1.4 establishes that the antecedent compression-map identity is not derivable from the allowed inputs because amplification naturality of theta is missing. Hence this node proves only the displayed conditional implication and does not prove the unconditional compressed-space identity or the root contract.
